fullPassage: How much time do you spend sitting per day? Studies have found that one-third of the global population aged fifteen years and older engage in insufficient physical activity. In particular, teenagers spend too much of their time sitting down and seldom do they engage in active physical activities on a regular basis. The scientific community has even coined the term “sitting disease” for this phenomenon in order to represent the harmful health effects that result from long periods of sitting. The longer you sit, the more exposed you are to the dangers of obesity, heart disease, diabetes, and even depression. Walking, according to health experts, is one of the safest, easiest, and cheapest forms of exercise to combat sitting disease. Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has other health benefits. You may already be aware of the health benefits of walking, such as bone strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and improved heart health. But did you know that walking can help lower your cravings for sugary foods? According to research by the University of Exeter, taking daily walks for fifteen minutes can cut chocolate consumption in half. This is because frequent physical activity can enhance brain function, making it easier to limit our consumption of sweet foods such as chocolate. Moreover, walking can keep you from getting sick during the cold and flu season. A study found that people who walked for at least twenty minutes a day, five days a week, had 43% fewer sick days than those who exercised once a week or less. And even if they did get sick, it was for a shorter period of time with milder symptoms. This is primarily due to the improved immune system that results from walking regularly. In addition to the physical benefits, walking has been found to improve our creativity. Researchers at Stanford University presented data on the association between walking and creativity. The participants who walked for five to sixteen minutes showed an average increase in creativity, compared to those who remained sitting. This was mainly because the areas of the brain responsible for learning and memory worked more efficiently when people walked. It is no wonder that Steve Jobs came up with some of his most brilliant ideas while walking, and much of his company’s design process was developed during walking meetings with his staff. Despite the importance and benefits of walking, as students, finding the time to include it in your daily lives may appear challenging or bothersome. Even when you have time, you may dismiss the thought of walking. Instead of walking, you might prefer to connect with friends on social media or watch TV at home. But walking can be fun. Here are some simple ways to make walking enjoyable for you. Get Your Groove On A “music walk” is a great way to make walking feel less like a workout. All you will need is a smartphone with a music streaming app and a good pair of walking shoes. Additionally, you can bring a pair of earphones in case other people are disturbed or annoyed by your music. You can create playlists for different moods or circumstances. Are you going for a walk at sunset by the lake? Create a playlist of calm and relaxing tunes to help you appreciate the peaceful environment. Going for a power walk to enjoy the autumn breeze? Fill your playlist with energetic songs that will motivate you to walk harder. So grab your phone, put on your walking shoes, and let the rhythm move you! Walk and Talk Having a walking buddy can really motivate you to lace up the sneakers if you feel lonely or bored when walking alone. When you make plans to walk with a friend, you are more likely to follow through since you do not want to let your friend down. Additionally, having someone to chat with can help you forget that you are even exercising, making the time fly by. You will find yourself so engaged in conversation that you will not even realize how far you have walked. Moreover, with a friend by your side, you will have someone to share the beauty of your surroundings with, making your walks more exciting and engaging. Make It a Challenge Set a goal for the number of steps you want to take per day or week, and then work toward it. Using a smartphone app, keep track of your daily steps. Increasing your step count over a few weeks would be challenging yet rewarding. You do not need to set aside time for this walking challenge. You can take part in the challenge by walking during your lunch break, taking the stairs instead of the elevator, or walking in place while brushing your teeth. You can even make walking a social media challenge and get others to join you. READ MORE Space Out! The human brain makes up only about 3% of our body weight but consumes approximately 20% of the body’s energy. It manages all our thoughts, behavior, feelings, and movements in daily life. An unhealthy brain can hinder body movements and disrupt normal living, even if the body is fine. Just like our bodies, our brains need rest to stay healthy. Spacing out, often referred to as a state of not having specific thoughts, can provide our busy brains with the chance to rest. Research shows that short periods of spacing out can enhance memory, learning, and creativity. For example, a study at Cornell University found that participants who rested and did nothing could recognize faces faster and more accurately than those engaged in other activities. Research in Japan also presented concrete evidence that resting without specific thoughts improved blood flow in the brain and facilitated swift idea generation. Spacing out does not mean that brain activity completely halts. In 2001, American scientist Dr. Marcus Raichle discovered that certain brain areas are active while people are spacing out with closed eyes and silent minds. Taking short breaks without specific thoughts activates these areas, allowing the brain to reset and function better. During these breaks, the brain organizes acquired information, creating an improved environment for engaging in dynamic activities. How about spacing out for a few minutes whenever you are very busy?

det.tip: 숫자(5~16분)와 뇌 영역(학습·기억)을 정확히 대조하세요.

ch: Stanford 대학 연구에서 걸은 참가자들은 앉아 있던 사람들보다 창의력이 평균적으로 감소했다.
참가자들은 30분 이상 걸었을 때 창의력이 높아졌다.
스티브 잡스는 직원들과 걸으며 회의하는 방식으로 회사 제품 디자인 작업의 상당 부분을 진행했다.
걸을 때 뇌에서 감정을 담당하는 영역이 더 효율적으로 작동했다.

questions.passage: Set a goal for the number of steps you want to take per day or week, and then ①<u>work</u> toward it. ②<u>Increasing</u> your step count over a few weeks would be challenging yet rewarding. You do not need to set aside time for this walking challenge. You can take part in the challenge by walking during your lunch break, ③<u>taking</u> the stairs instead of the elevator, or ④<u>to walk</u> in place while brushing your teeth.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ to walk → walking: 전치사 by 뒤 동명사들이 병렬로 연결되므로 walking
det.analysis:
✅ ① work: and then work toward it에서 앞의 명령문 Set과 병렬을 이루는 동사원형으로 적절
✅ ② Increasing: Increasing your step count ~ would be에서 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 동명사로 적절
✅ ③ taking: by walking ~, taking the stairs ~에서 walking과 병렬을 이루는 동명사로 적절
❌ ④ to walk → walking: 'by walking ~, taking ~, or ___ in place'는 전치사 by에 이어지는 동명사들이 or로 병렬 연결된 구조이다. walking, taking과 형태를 맞춰야 하므로 walking이 맞다 ← 정답
det.tip: 병렬구조는 형태를 일치시킵니다: by walking, taking, or walking

questions.passage: Walk and Talk Having a walking buddy can really motivate you to lace up the sneakers if you feel lonely or bored when walking alone.  When you make plans to walk with a friend, you are more likely to follow through since you do not want to let your friend down.  Additionally, having someone to chat with can help you forget that you are even exercising, making the time fly by.  You will find yourself so engaged in conversation that you will not even realize how far you have walked.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 혼자 걸을 때 느낄 수 있는 감정으로 '지루함(bored)'과 함께 언급된 것을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'Having a walking buddy can really motivate you to lace up the sneakers if you feel lonely or bored when walking alone.'에서 혼자 걸을 때 느낄 수 있는 감정으로 lonely(외로운)와 bored(지루한)를 들었다. 따라서 답은 lonely다.
det.tip: if you feel lonely or bored(외롭거나 지루할 때)에서 lonely를 찾습니다.

questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 친구와 걷기로 약속하면 실천할 가능성이 높아지는 이유는 친구를 '실망시키고' 싶지 않기 때문이다. '(친구를) 실망시키다'에 해당하는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (4단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'When you make plans to walk with a friend, you are more likely to follow through since you do not want to let your friend down.'에서 약속을 지키려는 이유가 친구를 '실망시키고(let your friend down)' 싶지 않기 때문이라고 했다.
det.tip: let ~ down(~을 실망시키다): let your friend down

questions.passage: The participants who walked for five to sixteen minutes showed an average increase in creativity, compared to those who remained sitting. This was mainly because the areas of the brain responsible for learning and memory worked more __________ (efficient) when people walked.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'the areas of the brain ~ worked more ___'에서 빈칸은 동사 worked를 수식하는 자리이다. 동사를 수식하는 것은 부사이므로 형용사 efficient를 부사 efficiently로 바꿔야 한다.
det.tip: 동사를 수식할 때는 부사: worked more efficiently(더 효율적으로 작동했다)

questions.passage: How much time do you spend sitting per day?  Studies have found that one-third of the global population aged fifteen years and older engage in insufficient physical activity.  In particular, teenagers spend too much of their time sitting down and seldom do they engage in active physical activities on a regular basis.  The scientific community has even coined the term “sitting disease” for this phenomenon in order to represent the harmful health effects that result from long periods of sitting.  The longer you sit, the more exposed you are to the dangers of obesity, heart disease, diabetes, and even depression.  Walking, according to health experts, is one of the safest, easiest, and cheapest forms of exercise to combat sitting disease.  Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has other health benefits.  You may already be aware of the health benefits of walking, such as bone strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and improved heart health.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① 앉아 있는 습관의 위험은 도입부 배경일 뿐 질병 '치료법'이 주제가 아님
② 걸음 수 기록은 걷기를 즐기는 여러 방법 중 하나일 뿐 전체 주제가 아님
③ 신체 활동 부족은 글을 시작하는 배경이며 사회적 원인 분석이 목적이 아님
④ 걷기가 주는 신체·면역·창의력상의 이점과, 음악 걷기·친구와 걷기·도전 등 걷기를 즐기는 방법을 함께 다루므로 글 전체를 포괄한다 ← 정답
det.tip: 글 전반부(이점)와 후반부(즐기는 방법)를 모두 포괄해야 주제입니다.

ch: 오래 앉아 있는 습관이 유발하는 여러 질병의 치료 방법
스마트폰 앱을 활용해 걸음 수를 기록하는 효과적인 방법
청소년의 신체 활동 부족 문제와 그 사회적 원인 분석
걷기의 다양한 건강·창의력상 이점과 걷기를 즐겁게 하는 방법

questions.passage: How much time do you spend sitting per day?  Studies have found that one-third of the global population aged fifteen years and older engage in insufficient physical activity.  In particular, teenagers spend too much of their time sitting down and seldom do they engage in active physical activities on a regular basis.  The scientific community has even coined the term “sitting disease” for this phenomenon in order to represent the harmful health effects that result from long periods of sitting.  The longer you sit, the more exposed you are to the dangers of obesity, heart disease, diabetes, and even depression.  Walking, according to health experts, is one of the safest, easiest, and cheapest forms of exercise to combat sitting disease.  Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has other health benefits.  You may already be aware of the health benefits of walking, such as bone strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and improved heart health.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① 글은 걷기가 sitting disease의 해로움을 막고 건강·면역·창의력에 이로우며, 이를 즐겁게 실천하는 방법을 제시하므로 핵심 메시지로 적절 ← 정답
② 초콜릿(단 음식) 이야기는 걷기의 여러 이점 중 하나의 예시일 뿐 요지가 아님
③ Steve Jobs는 창의력 향상의 예시로 잠깐 등장할 뿐 '걷기 회의 도입'이 요지가 아님
④ 감기·독감 예방은 걷기의 여러 이점 중 하나일 뿐 전체 요지가 아님
det.tip: 요지는 글 전체를 아우르는 핵심 주장입니다. '걷기의 이점 + 즐기는 방법'입니다.

ch: 걷기는 앉아서 생활하는 습관의 해로움을 막고 신체와 창의력에 도움을 주는 쉬운 운동이므로 일상에서 즐겁게 실천하는 것이 좋다.
단 음식 섭취를 줄이려면 반드시 규칙적인 유산소 운동을 병행해야 한다.
창의적인 아이디어를 얻으려면 Steve Jobs처럼 걷기 회의를 도입해야 한다.
감기와 독감을 예방하려면 매일 최소 20분 이상 걸어야만 한다.
